title: Crypto hierarchy, rotation, and SIEM export — runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook captures the operational design and step-by-step procedures for key lifecycle management (cloud KMS, HSM-backed keys, and customer BYOK), rotation patterns, and formatted audit export to the SIEM. It is intended for security engineers, platform engineers (private/dedicated), and on-call SREs who will perform rotations, evidence collection, and incident responses related to encryption-at-rest.

Non-goals:
- Specifying vendor-specific API docs (those are linked in the artifacts section).
- Replacing the Verified KMS onboarding checklist — this complements it with operational playbook material.

Overview of crypto hierarchy (recommended model):
- Root/Signer (offline or HSM-protected root key): only used to sign intermediate keys and for bootstrapping. Extremely high entropy, stored in FIPS-validated HSM or offline guard.
- Master Key (MK): KMS-managed single-purpose key used to encrypt/unwrap key-encryption-keys (KEKs). Rotated infrequently; stored in cloud KMS or HSM with strict RBAC.
- Key-Encryption Keys (KEKs): Per- tenancy (customer or environment) keys used to wrap Data Encryption Keys (DEKs). KEKs live in KMS/HSM and are subject to rotation policies independent of DEKs.
- Data Encryption Keys (DEKs): Short-lived keys used for envelope encryption of object data (S3, blockstore, DB column encryption). DEKs are generated by the service, encrypted with KEK, and stored alongside ciphertext.

Why envelope encryption: improved rotation and small blast radius — DEKs are cheap to rotate and do not require re-encrypting blobs when KEK rotates (only rewrap operation).

RBAC v2 for keys (mapping to roles):
- key-admin: create/delete/grant/revoke KEKs and manage key policy metadata. Should be restricted to Security Eng and Platform Admins. (Granting on a per-key resource basis.)
- key-operator: initiate rotate/rewrap operations, request key usage metrics, and run emergency revocations. Intended for SRE on-call + rotation automation service accounts.
- kms-viewer: read-only access to key metadata, audit entries, and rotation history; used by auditors and compliance reviewers.
- crypto-service (machine/account): service principal used by runtime to perform encrypt/decrypt operations — scoped to specific KEKs via least privilege.

Access controls and constraints:
- No human accounts with direct encrypt/decrypt rights on production KEKs unless explicitly approved and logged.
- All changes to key policy must require multi-approver workflow via ticket (JIRA-SEC or ServiceNow) with a signed justification field.

Rotation policy matrix (recommended default):
- Root/Signer: rotate only on explicit key compromise or re-keying cycle every 5+ years (with offline ceremony).
- Master Key (MK): 18–36 months, or immediately on suspected compromise.
- KEK (per-tenant): 6–12 months; automated rewrap of DEKs recommended during low-traffic windows.
- DEK: TTL 24 hours to 90 days based on workload sensitivity; for high-volume object stores, prefer short TTL (7–30 days) and frequent rewraps.

Rotation step-by-step (KEK rotation, automated):
1) Pre-checks:
   - Confirm current KEK metadata and last_rotation in KMS.
   - Verify successful snapshot/backup of key metadata snapshot (S3 location: s3://redwood-sec-key-metadata/yyyymmdd).
   - Check outstanding re-wrap tasks and in-flight writes; consult per-route write-latency dashboard.
   - Ensure automation runbook is in a healthy state (CI job green).
2) Create new KEK version in KMS/HSM using secure API. Tag version with rotation-correlation-id and timestamp.
3) Update service principal grants for the new key version (if using explicit version grants).
4) Enqueue rewrap job that will read ciphertext metadata, call KMS unwrap with old KEK -> DEK, then wrap DEK with new KEK, and write back wrapped value. Jobs are sharded and rate-limited to preserve latency SLOs.
5) Monitor rewrap progress, look for rewrap-failure counts and backoffs. Failures trigger automatic re-try with exponential backoff and eventual pager escalation to on-call.
6) After >= 95% rewrap completion, update key policy primary-version pointer to new KEK version. Keep old version alive for 30–90 days for rollback and emergency decrypt.
7) Post-ops: generate evidence bundle (audit logs, job run IDs, manifest of rewrapped object IDs) and export to secure evidence store.

Manual emergency rotation (compromise suspected):
- Immediate steps: set KEK to disabled state for new wraps (maintain unwrap to allow decrypts if needed), create incident ticket, notify CS/Legal if customer keys involved. For BYOK, escalate to customer contact according to contract.

BYOK specific flows and customer-supplied HSMs:
- Onboarding requires: customer intent form, key rollover policy acceptance, and KMS import key ceremony recorded in Confluence page.
- BYOK keys are treated as external-key IDs — Redwood stores only wrapped DEKs. Key operations with external HSM require dedicated connector host in customer VPC or HSM proxy with mutual-auth TLS.
- Rotation for BYOK: coordinate schedule with customer; do not perform unilateral rotation of a customer-supplied root. Documented SLA window must be observed.

Audit log schema (key events) — canonical fields (JSON log entry):
- timestamp: ISO8601 string
- event_type: one of [KEY_CREATE, KEY_ROTATE, KEY_VERSION_CREATE, KEY_DISABLE, KEY_ENABLE, KEY_DELETE, KEY_UNWRAP, KEY_WRAP, KEY_POLICY_CHANGE]
- resource_id: kms://<region>/<key-id>
- actor: <principal-id or service-account>
- actor_type: human|service|external-customer
- action_id: UUID (correlation across services)
- request_id: cloud-kms-request-id (if available)
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- reason: free text (failure reason / policy change note)
- correlation_tags: list of tags (rotation-correlation-id, ticket-id)
- old_version: version-id (if rotation)
- new_version: version-id (if rotation)
- rewrap_manifest_loc: s3://... or null
- sampled_trace: diagnostic trace id or null
- raw_event: raw provider event (if available)

Example log (single-line JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2024-11-05T22:14:31Z",
  "event_type": "KEY_ROTATE",
  "resource_id": "kms://us-east1/ke-abc123",
  "actor": "svc-key-rotation@redwood-infra",
  "actor_type": "service",
  "action_id": "b3a85d6f-4c2b-4a9d-8e1c-3d9f7a9d2fbb",
  "request_id": "cloudreq-9922",
  "outcome": "success",
  "reason": "scheduled-rotation",
  "correlation_tags": ["rotation-20241105", "JIRA-SEC-1290"],
  "old_version": "v1",
  "new_version": "v2",
  "rewrap_manifest_loc": "s3://redwood-sec-key-manifests/rewrap-20241105.json",
  "sampled_trace": "trace-7a9e",
  "raw_event": null
}

SIEM export mapping guidance:
- Ingest each canonical audit log into the SIEM as a single event with the following mapped fields: time, src_principal (actor), event_type, resource, correlation_id (action_id), outcome, tags, message.
- Enrich events with identity attributes from IAM (team, manager, risk_score) and with customer ids for tenant-scoped keys.
- Create SIEM detection rules for abnormal activity patterns:
  - Multiple KEY_UNWRAP calls from different service principals for the same resource within a short window.
  - New key-version creation without a preceding JIRA ticket tag.
  - KEK rotates outside maintenance window.
  - Unexpected external-customer key access from internal VMs.

Evidence automation (post-rotation evidence bundle):
- Components to collect automatically after a rotation or emergency action:
  - Audit log slice covering action_id and +/- 24 hours.
  - Rewrap manifest (list of objects rewrapped and shard ids).
  - KMS provider raw response payloads and request IDs.
  - CI/CD job run ids and artifacts (automation run logs).
  - Signed PDF of rotation approvers (if manual approvals present).
- Automation job will package the above into a signed tarball, compute a SHA256, upload to s3://redwood-sec-evidence/<action_id>/evidence.tar.gz and emit an evidence-created audit event.

Testing, validation and rollback:
- Canary run: pick a low-traffic tenant and perform a KEK rotate + rewrap. Validate decrypt success on sampled objects for 48 hours. Use automated smoke tests (github.com/redwood-infra/tests/key-rotate-canary).
- Rollback: if rewrap fails en masse, revert primary-version pointer to previous version and abort further wrap jobs. Keep failure manifest for investigation.

Monitoring and observability:
- Key metrics to publish: rewrap_progress_percent, rewrap_error_rate, key_usage_per_minute, key_latency_p50/p90/p99 for wrap/unwrap calls, key_policy_change_count.
- Dashboards: per-region key counters, tenant-impact view, and a security incidents dashboard that surfaces any disabled keys or rapid version churn.

Operational playbook checklist (pre-rotation):
- [ ] Confirm maintenance window and customer notifications (if tenant scoped).
- [ ] Snapshot key metadata.
- [ ] Ensure rewrap jobs have capacity and throttles configured.
- [ ] Backup evidence store writable.

Post-rotation checklist:
- [ ] Rewrap >= 95% completed or documented exception list.
- [ ] Evidence tarball produced and verified.
- [ ] Post-rotation smoke tests green.
- [ ] Update key inventory and rotation calendar.

Compromise handling (short runbook):
1) Immediately mark key as disabled for new wraps and log action.
2) Create incident ticket with correlation_id and contact list.
3) If customer key (BYOK), notify customer per contract and follow agreed escalation.
4) Start forensic capture: full audit slice, host traces, and rewrap manifest.
5) If necessary, perform emergency rewrap to new KEK and reject old version; expedite evidence export for compliance.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require HSM for all MKs by default or only high-sensitivity tenants? (propose: high-sensitivity and enterprise with SLA >$Xk/month)
- Retention policy for old key versions beyond rollback window (30/90/365 days?)
- Integration point for RBAC v2 authorization checks in the KMS proxy — pre-check or delegated to provider?

Next steps (action items):
- Lina: draft BYOK onboarding form for customer agreements (due 2024-11-20).
- Diego: implement SIEM enrichment pipeline prototype (P0) and push PR.
- Samir: add rotation canary to infra tests and schedule monthly runs.

References and links:
- KMS provider docs (internal vault): CONFLUENCE-SEC/KMS-Provider-APIs
- Rewrap job implementation: github.com/redwood-infra/rewrap-service (PR-487 linked above)
- Evidence automation template: CONFLUENCE-SEC/Evidence-Automation-Template
- Incident escalation contact list: CONFLUENCE-SEC/Incident-Contacts

Notes and contextual snippets (working):
- Consider adding rate-limit bucketing per-tenant to rewrap workers to avoid noisy-tenant storms.
- We should index rewrap-manifests by tenant and time for quick e-discovery.
- Long-term: explore native HSM signing for root key ceremonies and publish an offline attestation record.

Document history:
